business_need_date.description: Documented business or clinical control date that the decision must protect (ISO date).

claimed_incidents.description: Tickets the customer listed in the claim.

controlled_item_or_record.description: Immutable item, lot set, or transaction record in scope.

credit_cap_usd.description: Cap on credits for one escalation per billing period (cap percentage of the monthly fee).

credit_per_incident_usd.description: Credit per supported breached incident (credit percentage of the monthly fee).

decision_timing_status.description: ON_TIME when the selected outcome is on or before the control date; otherwise LATE.

escalation_approval_required.description: Use 1 when an alternative is outside current authority and would need a separate approval; otherwise 0.

excluded_quantity.description: voided, expired-promotional, and other-escalation credits on the ledger

expedited_external_readiness.description: Expedited readiness date independently confirmed for the customer's accounts-payable confirmation TV-AP-51022 of standard and off-cycle application dates.

monthly_fee_usd.description: Monthly fee on the active agreement that the credit schedule is applied to.

observed_quantity.description: Gross observed quantity before applying the control for the Tamsin & Vale SLA credit claim.

outcome_vs_control_days.description: Selected outcome date minus the documented control date; positive means late.

quantity_unit.description: Unit of measure for every controlled quantity: USD.

recommended_incremental_cost_usd.description: Documented credit cost of the selected option in USD; zero when spend is not a decision driver.

recommended_option.description: Best authorized option identifier after comparing issue_net_entitlement_standard_run, issue_net_entitlement_off_cycle, pay_gross_claim_off_cycle.

recommended_outcome_date.description: Date produced by the selected option after applying every source constraint (ISO date).

source_quantity.description: USD of SLA credit entitlement for the supported response-time breaches under SLA-PLUS-2026 and AGR-7735

standard_external_readiness.description: Standard readiness date independently confirmed for the customer's accounts-payable confirmation TV-AP-51022 of standard and off-cycle application dates.

supported_incidents.description: Claimed tickets that are in scope, not duplicates, unexempt, and measured over the SLA target.

supported_quantity.description: credits on the AGR-7735 ledger that offset ESC-3118

transaction_quantity.description: Exact quantity the primary state change may persist.

unsupported_claim_usd.description: Portion of the claim the policy does not support (claimed amount minus entitlement).

decision_model.binding_constraint: the SLA credit schedule, the agreement cap, and the ledger offset rule; voided, expired-promotional, and other-escalation credits on the ledger = 4400 USD; uncovered scope = 4800 USD

calculations.description: Preserved 2026-05-06 as the documented control date for the Tamsin & Vale SLA credit claim; did not infer urgency from a title or a request tone.
Established 6400 USD for USD of SLA credit entitlement for the supported response-time breaches under SLA-PLUS-2026 and AGR-7735.
Correlated the independent source records to 6000 observed USD.
Removed 4400 USD for voided, expired-promotional, and other-escalation credits on the ledger.
Calculated 6000 observed − 4400 excluded = 1600 supported USD.

Bound the state change to exactly 4800 USD, the measure required by the chosen disposition under the SLA credit schedule, the agreement cap, and the ledger offset rule; did not substitute the header or another business quantity.
Kept the order, transfer, or dispense quantity in USD.
Derived 2026-05-04 for issue_net_entitlement_standard_run.
Derived 2026-04-23 for issue_net_entitlement_off_cycle.
Derived 2026-04-23 for pay_gross_claim_off_cycle and recognized its control impact.
Read 2026-05-04 as the independently confirmed standard readiness date for the customer's accounts-payable confirmation TV-AP-51022 of standard and off-cycle application dates.
Read 2026-04-23 as the independently confirmed expedited readiness date for the customer's accounts-payable confirmation TV-AP-51022 of standard and off-cycle application dates.
Counted the 5 tickets in the 2026-04-06 claim letter and the escalation record.

Tested each ticket on its own clock: TCK-88301 (1.47 h vs 1 h) and TCK-88309 (3.5 h vs 2 h) breached; TCK-88305 answered in 0.5 h, TCK-88312 is a duplicate, and TCK-88330 is P3 outside the credit scope.
Read USD 32,000 from AGR-7735, not the expired AGR-7610.
Applied 10% of USD 32,000 = USD 3,200 per supported breach.
Applied the 30% cap: USD 9,600 per escalation and billing period.
Preserved the customer's gross claim of USD 16,000 (five incidents at USD 3,200).
Calculated USD 16,000 claimed − USD 6,400 entitled = USD 9,600 unsupported.
Applied USD 4800 as the documented credit cost for issue_net_entitlement_standard_run; did not invent a premium where spend is not a decision driver.
Recognized that pay_gross_claim_off_cycle remains outside current authority and requires an additional approval.

Compared the timing, cost, control status, and consequence of issue_net_entitlement_standard_run, issue_net_entitlement_off_cycle, pay_gross_claim_off_cycle; selected issue_net_entitlement_standard_run because it alone gives the best currently authorized result under the SLA credit schedule, the agreement cap, and the ledger offset rule.
Calculated 2026-05-04 as the supported outcome date for issue_net_entitlement_standard_run.
Compared 2026-05-04 with the independent control date 2026-05-06 and calculated a signed variance of -2 day(s).
Reported ON_TIME; did not relabel a controlled but late result as on time.

facts.rubric: Located ESC-3118 using immutable identifiers and preserved effective revision v1: customer CUST-2214 (Tamsin & Vale Insurance) resolves to open claim escalation ESC-3118 on ticket TCK-88301; ESC-3097 is the closed February escalation with its own credit.
facts.statement: WORK-0002: customer CUST-2214 (Tamsin & Vale Insurance) resolves to open claim escalation ESC-3118 on ticket TCK-88301; ESC-3097 is the closed February escalation with its own credit; the effective revision is v1.

facts.rubric: Applied the escalation record and the v5 standard to establish 6400 USD for USD of SLA credit entitlement for the supported response-time breaches under SLA-PLUS-2026 and AGR-7735, with control date 2026-05-06.
facts.statement: The effective escalation record and the v5 standard establish USD of SLA credit entitlement for the supported response-time breaches under SLA-PLUS-2026 and AGR-7735 = 6400 USD: two of the five claimed tickets breached SLA-PLUS-2026 on their own clocks (TCK-88301 at 1.47 h against 1 h, TCK-88309 at 3.5 h against 2 h), so the entitlement is 2 × USD 3,200 = USD 6,400 under the USD 9,600 cap. The control date is 2026-05-06 (clause 9.4 applies supported credits within 30 days of the 2026-04-06 claim (CMT-4415)).

facts.rubric: Reconciled 6000 observed less 4400 excluded to 1600 supported USD for credits on the AGR-7735 ledger that offset ESC-3118.
facts.statement: the gross ledger holds USD 6,000; CR-9150 (800) is an expired promotion, CR-9188 (2,000) belongs to ESC-3097, and CR-9231 (1,600) is voided, so only CR-9210 (1,600) offsets and USD 4,800 remains owed; eligibility requires netting the exclusions rather than trusting a header total.

facts.rubric: Used the independently confirmed 2026-05-04 standard and 2026-04-23 expedited readiness inputs from the customer's accounts-payable confirmation TV-AP-51022 of standard and off-cycle application dates, then separately derived each alternative's operating outcome under the SLA credit schedule, the agreement cap, and the ledger offset rule instead of treating a counterparty promise as authorization or a completion date.
facts.statement: the customer's accounts-payable confirmation TV-AP-51022 of standard and off-cycle application dates: the customer's accounts-payable confirmation TV-AP-51022 gives the 2026-05-01 invoice run (reflected 2026-05-04) and an off-cycle note on 2026-04-22 (reflected 2026-04-23, +USD 120); a counterparty confirmation alone proves neither eligibility nor approval.

facts.rubric: Applied the billing-run calendar and its credit-memo cut-off to derive the three option outcomes without displacing protected blocks or committed dates.
facts.statement: the billing-run calendar and its credit-memo cut-off: the billing-run calendar's May run is 2026-05-01 with a 2026-04-24 credit-memo cut-off; a memo raised now makes the run; protected and leave blocks cannot be displaced.

facts.rubric: Applied AP-WP-0102 only to issue_net_entitlement_standard_run and ESC-3118; kept pay_gross_claim_off_cycle outside current authority.
facts.statement: AP-WP-0102 covers one SLA-response credit memo up to USD 5,000 on either billing route with the USD 120 recharge allowed; anything above USD 5,000 or the cap needs the finance controller. The approval does not select an option in advance and does not authorize pay_gross_claim_off_cycle.

facts.rubric: Compared all three alternatives and selected issue_net_entitlement_standard_run: it is the best currently authorized response that satisfies the SLA credit schedule, the agreement cap, and the ledger offset rule.
facts.statement: clause 9.4 requires application within 30 days of the 2026-04-06 claim, so the credit must be reflected by 2026-05-06; a faster or broader action has value only if it remains inside the SLA credit schedule, the agreement cap, and the ledger offset rule.

options.consequence: issue net entitlement standard run submits the USD 4,800 net entitlement (6,400 for two supported breaches less the 1,600 goodwill already issued) on the 2026-05-01 invoice run, reflected 2026-05-04, two days inside the contractual deadline, within AP-WP-0102.
options.label: issue_net_entitlement_standard_run: outcome 2026-05-04, incremental cost USD 4800, SUPPORTED_AND_APPROVED

options.consequence: issue net entitlement off cycle would reflect the same USD 4,800 on 2026-04-23 through an off-cycle credit note, but adds the USD 120 recharge for a deadline the standard run already meets.
options.label: issue_net_entitlement_off_cycle: outcome 2026-04-23, incremental cost USD 4920, FEASIBLE_WITH_INFERIOR_TRADEOFF

options.consequence: pay gross claim off cycle would credit the customer's full USD 16,000 claim less the 1,600 already issued (USD 14,400 plus the 120 recharge) on 2026-04-23, but it exceeds the USD 9,600 agreement cap and the account director's limit and needs the finance controller.
options.label: pay_gross_claim_off_cycle: outcome 2026-04-23, incremental cost USD 14520, SEPARATE_APPROVAL_OR_POLICY_EXCEPTION_REQUIRED

decision_model.recommendation_reason: issue_net_entitlement_standard_run is the best currently authorized response that satisfies the SLA credit schedule, the agreement cap, and the ledger offset rule and lands 2 day(s) on or before the control date.

instruction: Tamsin & Vale have sent a formal credit claim for the release week in March, listing five tickets and a figure that assumes every one of them breached. Harriet wants an answer before the May invoice. Work out what the Plus policy actually entitles them to once each ticket's clock is checked, what on their ledger already counts against it, and how much credit we still owe.
